title: The Copper Letter
premise: In 1893, on the storm-battered coast of Cornwall, widowed lighthouse keeper Odile Eastwick finds a copper-sealed letter washed ashore, addressed to a family she once served as a governess—a family now entangled in a treasonous smuggling plot with a French arms dealer. The letter is a promise made in peacetime by her late husband's brother, and honoring it means sheltering the family's hunted daughter while authorities close in. As the great storms of that year batter the coast, Odile must choose between her hard-won invisibility and the found family she never expected to keep. In the end, she burns the letter, testifies against the corrupt magistrate who orchestrated the plot, and keeps the lighthouse—and the girl—as her own.
about_author: Marguerite Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse keepers' logs along the Cornish coast before turning to fiction. She writes historical novels about ordinary people caught in the machinery of power.

chapters.title: The Salt Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Establishes her meticulous, solitary routine tending the light after her husband's drowning two years prior. A violent autumn storm washes debris ashore, including a strange copper cylinder. Emotional beat: grief managed through order, about to be disrupted.

chapters.title: Copper and Wax
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She pries open the cylinder: a letter from her late husband's brother Thomas to the Vane family, promising refuge 'should the tide turn.' The name chills her—the Vanes are in the newspapers, accused of treason. Beat: dread blooming under duty.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Visit
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Magistrate Corvane arrives asking questions about wreckage and 'papers,' his charm thin over menace. She lies for the first time since her wedding day. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance; the letter hidden in the oil store.

chapters.title: What Thomas Promised
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Odile's POV. Her years as Vane governess, Thomas's idealism, her marriage, and the promise she witnessed him make. Beat: love against duty established—she owes the Vanes something older than law.

chapters.title: A Girl at the Door
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. During the worst storm yet, sixteen-year-old Sylvie Vane appears half-drowned at the lighthouse door, fleeing London after her father's arrest. Beat: the promise comes due; Odile takes her in without letting herself feel it.

chapters.title: Two Keepers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. Sylvie's chapters show terror and sharp intelligence; she notices everything, including Corvane's men watching the cove. Odile teaches her the lamps. Beat: wary friction softening into rhythm.

chapters.title: The Wreckers' Light
chapters.summary: Sylvie's POV. They discover someone has been showing false lights to lure ships—smugglers running French arms, using the Vanes' name as cover. Beat: the plot is bigger than one family; corruption reaches the magistrate himself.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Corvane returns, offering protection in exchange for the letter and testimony against the Vanes. He reveals Thomas died in custody months ago. Beat: grief and rage; she refuses, and knows he won't forgive it.

chapters.title: The Fisherman's Net
chapters.summary: Sylvie's POV. Local fisherman Bram Trelawney, who owed Thomas his life, becomes an ally, hiding supplies and news. The village quietly closes ranks around the women. Beat: found family taking root among strangers.

chapters.title: Intercepted
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She copies the letter and sends word to a sympathetic solicitor in Plymouth via Bram's boat. A storm delays the boat; a customs officer searches it and finds nothing—but reports 'unusual traffic' at the light. Beat: time running out.

chapters.title: What Sylvie Saw
chapters.summary: Sylvie's POV. She confesses she saw her father take bribes—not innocence, but complicity—and fears she deserves her fate. Odile tells her about her own failures as a wife and keeper. Beat: guilt met with grace; trust sealed.

chapters.title: The False Flame
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Corvane's men sabotage the lamp mechanism during a gale, hoping a dark light will justify seizing the station. Odile and Sylvie keep the light burning by hand all night, rotating the lens themselves. Beat: triumph forged in exhaustion.

chapters.title: Bram's Bargain
chapters.summary: Bram's POV (single departure). He bargains with a smuggler captain for information on Corvane's arms shipments, trading silence for evidence. Beat: loyalty tested; he chooses the women over the village's uneasy peace.

chapters.title: The Solicitor's Reply
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Plymouth responds: the solicitor will act, but only if Odile surrenders the original letter and testifies—an act that exposes her to charges of harboring a traitor's daughter. Beat: the cost of doing right made explicit.

chapters.title: Corvane Closes In
chapters.summary: Sylvie's POV. Soldiers quarter in the village inn; Corvane announces the lighthouse will be inspected. Sylvie offers to surrender herself to save Odile. Odile slaps the idea down harder than she means to. Beat: love against duty inverted—each willing to be sacrificed.

chapters.title: The Storm of the Century
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The great storm hits at full force. A ship founders on the rocks—carrying Corvane's arms shipment, lured by his own false light gone wrong. Beat: chaos as nature indicts the corrupt.

chapters.title: Wreckage and Witness
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Rescue efforts through the dawn; villagers see the arms crates and the false-light apparatus among the wreckage. Corvane attempts to blame the Vanes publicly. Beat: the truth surfacing whether anyone wants it or not.

chapters.title: The Copper Letter Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Sylvie's POV. Before the assembled village and a naval investigator, Odile reads Thomas's letter aloud—her promise, kept. Sylvie claims her father's crimes as hers to answer for; the village answers instead with shelter. Beat: catharsis; the promise fulfilled in public.

chapters.title: Corvane's Fall
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The naval inquiry, armed with Bram's evidence and the wrecked shipment, turns on Corvane. He offers Odile a final bribe; she burns the original letter in front of him—'promises aren't evidence, they're debts paid.' Beat: power's corruption undone by refusal.

chapters.title: Pardons and Partings
chapters.summary: Sylvie's POV. Sylvie is cleared; a distant aunt offers her a life in Bath, respectable and safe. She almost goes. Beat: the ache of chosen family facing its first real test.

chapters.title: The Second Keeper
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Sylvie returns on the morning mail coach, having sent the aunt a polite refusal. Officially appointed assistant keeper—the first woman so named on this coast. Beat: quiet joy; invisibility traded for belonging.

chapters.title: Light Over Water
chapters.summary: Shared POV, closing. One year later: the storms have passed, the lamp is steady, Bram fishes the cove, and a new copper cylinder—this one a letter of their own writing—is sealed and shelved, a promise for whoever needs it next. Beat: peace earned, legacy begun.
